1. If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide#your-first-contribution and developer guide https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/development.md#development-guide

**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespace from that line:
>
> /kind api-change
> /kind bug
> /kind cleanup
> /kind deprecation
> /kind design
> /kind documentation
> /kind failing-test
> /kind feature
> /kind flake

/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Metrics improvement in kubelet based on production experience at Pinterest:
1. revised histogram buckets and tags in pod (pod startup durations, container count, pod worker durations, pod evictions)
2. added metrics about image pull, image cache hit

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #88378

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
Kubelet Metrics: revised histogram buckets and tags in pod related metrics (pod startup durations, container count, pod worker durations, pod evictions), added metrics for image pull and image cache hit
```

/cc @yujuhong @dchen1107 @Random-Liu

Hi @zhan849. Thanks for your PR.

I'm waiting for a [kubernetes](https://github.com/orgs/kubernetes/people) member to verify that this patch is reasonable to test. If it is, they should reply with `/ok-to-test` on its own line. Until that is done, I will not automatically test new commits in this PR, but the usual testing commands by org members will still work. Regular contributors should [join the org](https://git.k8s.io/community/community-membership.md#member) to skip this step.

Once the patch is verified, the new status will be reflected by the `ok-to-test` label.

I understand the commands that are listed [here](https://go.k8s.io/bot-commands?repo=kubernetes%2Fkubernetes).

<details>

Instructions for interacting with me using PR comments are available [here](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md).  If you have questions or suggestions related to my behavior, please file an issue against the [kubernetes/test-infra](https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/issues/new?title=Prow%20issue:) repository.
</details>
/assign @dchen1107

> /ok-to-test
> 
> Does this pr change the behavior for existing metrics?

@mattjmcnaughton I'd consider changing buckets and adding labels as "behavior changes", but since all metrics are in Alpha stage this shall be acceptable?
/retest

> > /ok-to-test
> > Does this pr change the behavior for existing metrics?
> 
> @mattjmcnaughton I'd consider changing buckets and adding labels as "behavior changes", but since all metrics are in Alpha stage this shall be acceptable?

ooh great question... I must admit I don't know.

cc @RainbowMango who I believe has worked on diffs in this realm in the past :)

Yeah, Alpha metrics means you can update by anytime. But we also should be cautious, because some of these may be used extensively. 

/cc @dashpole

> I'm curious what others think, but I would prefer keeping the carnality of metrics on this endpoint bounded. Metrics on this endpoint are designed to diagnose issues with the kubelet, rather than problems with workloads, which is why we have refrained from adding workload information (e.g. namespace and image) in the past.

I agree with @dashpole, this looks problematic. If the node never dies, then we can expect this dimension to grow indefinitely causing the kubelet to OOM eventually.
/hold

/sig instrumentation 
/cc @brancz @RainbowMango

>

@logicalhan @dashpole sounds good to me. I can keep the bucket change and remove the pod namespace related info. For image pull, since this is the only place users would have visibility, what doo you guys think about keeping it here for pragmatic reason?

> @logicalhan @dashpole sounds good to me. I can keep the bucket change and remove the pod namespace related info. For image pull, since this is the only place users would have visibility, what doo you guys think about keeping it here for pragmatic reason?

Don't we have access to image pull data in events? The unbounded nature of the image names makes this very undesirable as a metric.

> > @logicalhan @dashpole sounds good to me. I can keep the bucket change and remove the pod namespace related info. For image pull, since this is the only place users would have visibility, what doo you guys think about keeping it here for pragmatic reason?
> 
> Don't we have access to image pull data in events? The unbounded nature of the image names makes this very undesirable as a metric.

getting number from events could be less desired as as far as I remember, events are mostly for human debugging purposes and not for programmatic usages.

The current upstream has data about CRI calls, its just image pull latency is yet a different magnitude as other calls so current buckets makes very little sense in debugging.

Besides bucket change, due to the large variation of image size a single company could have, not labeling things up could also have the data less practical. Can we make the assumption, at least during alpha stage, **_that image name (without tag) can be bounded in a cluster_** and we label image pull latency by image name only?

> Can we make the assumption, at least during alpha stage, that image name (without tag) can be bounded in a cluster and we label image pull latency by image name only?

For metrics stability, Alpha only refers to the backwards-compatibility guarantees that exist for a particular metric.  In other contexts in kubernetes (feature gates & enhancements), alpha means that it is disabled by default, which allows such features to do things that would normally not be permitted.  We will want to bound cardinality for all metrics, including alpha metrics.

> We will want to bound cardinality for all metrics, including alpha metrics.

sounds good, so I will keep the PR limited to:
- new buckets for existing pods related latency (no label change)
- new metrics for image pull (no label at all)

issue_context.title: Kubelet metrics improvement
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
1. Currently we are using default bucket for many histograms inside kubelet, however, for stats that can span mostly from seconds to minutes, we can have different buckets to make numbers more meaningful
2. it'd be very useful if runtime operations has specific metrics for images - this helps infra teams to detect inefficient images (those constantly needs pulling, or takes long time to pull) and provide feedbacks to related teams
3. pod related metrics that has a user side significance (pod startup latency, eviction, etc) shall add namespace tag


**Why is this needed**:
explained above

/assign zhan849
/sig node
